taxonomic_note: Current Kew POWO accepts Oenothera macrocarpa subsp. macrocarpa. Historical Texas usage under Oenothera missouriensis or O. macrocarpa var. missouriensis folds here.
look_here_first: Look for the low spreading habit, huge yellow evening-opening flowers, and especially the very large winged fruits. It is a dry limestone-prairie plant, not a tall riverbank primrose.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Master Plant Pool marks Oenothera macrocarpa Hays-local. Travis — UT Travis County Onagraceae index includes O. macrocarpa var. macrocarpa, matching the current subspecies concept. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a dedicated treatment of O. macrocarpa subsp. macrocarpa.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Historical var. macrocarpa / missouriensis names are mapped to the current accepted subspecies only when taxonomically equivalent.

best_field_traits: low perennial, often spreading to ascending
dry calcareous prairie, limestone glades, and rocky hillsides
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The oversized winged capsule is the strongest field clue. O. jamesii is taller and riparian; O. patriciae has much smaller white-to-rose gaura-like flowers and narrow fruits.
